# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

Americans for Propriety is a civic project. We expect contributors to act with the same standards of conduct we ask of public officials: respect for the people you're addressing, rigor about the claims you're making, and good faith in disagreement.

## Standards

Examples of behavior that strengthens this community:

- Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward others.
- Engaging with the strongest version of opposing views, not the easiest (Principle 04).
- Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback.
- Acknowledging mistakes, fixing them, and crediting people who pointed them out.
- Focusing on what is best for the project and the people it serves.

Examples of behavior that will get you removed from this community:

- Personal attacks, harassment, intimidation, or sustained disruption.
- Bad-faith argument: misrepresenting another contributor's position, demanding proof of premises stated in good faith, or arguing without intent to be persuaded by evidence.
- Trolling, insulting comments, or political invective unrelated to the substance of a contribution.
- Publishing others' private information without explicit permission.
- Sexualized language or imagery, or unwelcome sexual attention.
- Conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting.

Disagreement on the merits — about a policy position, a sourcing standard, an editorial choice, an architectural decision — is welcome and expected. The line is between disagreeing with what someone wrote and treating them as a target.

## Scope

This Code applies to all project spaces: issues, pull requests, discussions, the project's repositories on GitHub, and any official communication channels (email lists, Slack/Discord if added later, in-person meetings if held). It also applies when an individual is officially representing the project — e.g., posting from an Americans for Propriety account or speaking at an event in that capacity.

## Enforcement

Reports of unacceptable behavior should be sent to <hello@americansforpropriety.org>. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly. The maintainers are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter.

Project maintainers may, at their discretion:

- Ask a contributor to revise a comment, PR description, or issue.
- Lock a thread that has stopped being productive.
- Issue a warning, in private or in public depending on severity.
- Temporarily ban a contributor from project spaces.
- Permanently ban a contributor for severe or repeated violations.

We will explain enforcement decisions when we make them, except when doing so would compromise a reporter's privacy.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), version 2.1, with revisions reflecting the project's editorial values.
